subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should ACP preserve parallel execution for distinct child sessions while fixing only proven launch-readiness failures, or should OpenClaw add an explicit concurrency gate for ACP child spawns?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally allow distinct ACP sessions to run in parallel, so changing that behavior cannot be selected safely without maintainer intent and live evidence.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and prove the bug
options.body: Run a current ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke and fix the specific launch/readiness failure if it reproduces, leaving distinct-session parallelism intact.

options.title: Gate ACP concurrency explicitly
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved concurrency gate or operator setting only if live proof shows ACPX/Claude cannot safely handle rapid distinct child spawns.

options.title: Close after no current repro
options.body: Close only if a current latest-release or current-main live smoke shows both rapid ACP child spawns reliably produce output.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and prove the bug
recommendation.body: Run a current ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke and fix the specific launch/readiness failure if it reproduces, leaving distinct-session parallelism intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame for the inspected ACP spawn and manager paths points to recent work by steipete, and the decision involves preserving or changing current concurrency behavior.
